findings.title: Resource leak: opened file not closed
findings.body: The file opened on line 7 is appended to `_open_reports` but never closed, so every call to `read_report` leaks a file handle. The context manager (`with`) used in the original code on lines 5–6 ensured proper cleanup. Append the file to `_open_reports` only after reading and close it explicitly, or use a context manager to guarantee closure.
findings.suggestion:
with path.open(encoding="utf-8") as report:
        content = report.read()
    _open_reports.append(report)
    return content

findings.title: Global mutable list `_open_reports` violates encapsulation
findings.body: A module-level mutable list `_open_reports` exposes internal state and invites misuse. It is not cleared between calls, so `_open_reports` grows indefinitely, risking memory leaks. Encapsulate the list in a function or class and provide controlled access (e.g., append only after reading and close immediately).
findings.suggestion:
_open_reports: list[TextIO] = []

def read_report(path: Path) -> str:
    with path.open(encoding="utf-8") as report:
        content = report.read()
    _open_reports.append(report)
    return content

summary.problem: The change introduces a resource leak and a global mutable list that can grow indefinitely.
summary.done_well: The new code attempts to track opened files, showing awareness of resource management.
